text: <blocked>perform_expensive_operations (which the ABI requires calling directly, and which long_exec also calls 2000 times per invocation) runs 100 rounds per array element of x=3x+7; x^=x>>3; x-=x<<1; x=x/2+x%7. The xor-shift step always produces a non-negative value, so x<<1 in the next line never shifts a negative operand, but that operand's magnitude grows by roughly 1.5x every round regardless of the starting value: hand-simulating from x=0 (the value every element of the zero-initialized global array starts at) gives |x| = 3,1,6,9,11,18,22,35,58 at rounds 0-8, and this geometric growth crosses INT_MAX/3 by roughly round 50 - well inside the fixed 100-round inner loop, and far short of the 2000x repetition long_exec applies on top. Signed integer overflow (undefined behavior) in x*3+7 or x<<1 is therefore essentially unavoidable for most of the 262144 elements on the very first call to perform_expensive_operations, for any array contents and irrespective of the seed passed to long_exec, since seed only changes rand()'s initial values, not the transform's structural divergence. Because both listed symbols must be called and neither can be called without triggering this overflow, no driver satisfying the "never trigger undefined behavior / sanitizer-clean" requirement can be written for this unit.</blocked>
